diagnostic_evidence.quote: the family of all linear sampling algorithms $S_k^X$ in $L_2(U,X;\mu)$ of the form \eqref{S_k} with $k \le n$

issues.failure_explanation: Item (iii) asserts the chain rho_n(B) << sup_v ||v - S_{c_3 n} v|| << M N n^{-1/q}. The middle term is the error of a least-squares algorithm that uses c_3 n >= 3284 n samples, so it only bounds rho_{c_3 n}, not rho_n. Since rho_n is non-increasing in n, rho_n >= rho_{c_3 n}, and the first inequality does not follow from the definitions. The proof only transfers the upper bounds of Theorem thm:leastsquaresbounds and never addresses this inequality. The final rate for rho_n is still true, but it needs a separate step: monotonicity plus regularity of the n^{-1/q} rate, applied at n/c_3. The same flawed chain is repeated in the infinite-dimensional version.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the first inequality as rho_{c_3 n} <= sup_v ||v - S_{c_3 n} v||. Then deduce rho_n << M N n^{-1/q} from the monotonicity of rho_n and the polynomial form of the rate, using n/c_3 in place of n.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed chain in (iii) is unsupported as written. The bound on the n-sample sampling width rho_n is not derived from the proof as given. The stated rate for rho_n is nevertheless obtainable by a short extra argument.
issues.title: Sampling width with n samples bounded by the error of an algorithm that uses c_3 n samples
issues.why_classification: The repair is a short local fix using monotonicity and the n^{-1/q} form of the rate. The final rate, the method and the scope are all preserved.

issues.failure_explanation: The weight in (sigma_s) factorizes as sigma_s^2 = prod_j sum_{t=0}^{eta} C(s_j,t) rho_j^{2t}. For s = k e_1 this gives sigma^2 <= C k^eta. Hence sum_k sigma_{k e_1}^{-q} >= c sum_k k^{-eta q/2}, which diverges whenever eta q <= 2. For example, q = 1 and eta = 1 or 2 gives ||sigma^{-1}||_{ell_q} = infinity. The lognormal lemma claims ||sigma^{-1}||_{ell_q} <= N < infinity for every eta in N and every 0 < q < infinity. The holomorphic lemma claims it for an arbitrary eta in N with q = p/(1-p). Both statements are false for small eta, and a condition such as eta > 2/q is missing. The weighted summability in these lemmas is what feeds Theorem varrho_n><, and the condition eta > 2/q is not stated in either lemma or in the theorems built on them.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis eta > 2/q (for example eta = floor(2/q)+1) to both lemmas. Carry it into the log-normal and holomorphic sampling theorems, including the condition involving sqrt(eta!).
issues.overall_effect: As stated, the hypotheses of both lemmas admit values of eta for which the conclusion is false. The log-normal branch of the sampling theorem and the holomorphic sampling theorem inherit the unconstrained eta. The holomorphic theorem's condition with sqrt(eta!) is also stated for an unspecified eta. The affine branch, which uses a different weight, is unaffected.
issues.title: Weights sigma_s have ell_q-summable inverses only if eta > 2/q, but the lemmas allow any eta
issues.why_classification: A standard local hypothesis on the free parameter eta repairs the statements. The method, the rates n^{-1/q} and the scope (0 < p < 2/3, q < 2) all survive.
